clue.text: In direction of current ambition, securing private street

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast, so 'ambition' holds 'private street' inside it

blocks.note: an ambition is a dream you hope to realise
private, as in your own room
standard abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: Someone's ambition carried along by the tide, with a private street in the frame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' suggests present-day, as in current ambition, but it is the flow of water; 'private' is the possessive sense, your own.
explanation.definitionFit: Travelling with the flow of a river or tide is going downstream, in the same direction the water moves.

clue.text: Colourant below standard? Certainly time to go into that

indicators.note: the pair 'certainly' and 'time' must go into the word for 'below standard'

blocks.note: duff is British slang for useless or of poor quality
a firm agreement
standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A dye maker judges a colour substandard and decides it is time to investigate.
explanation.walkthrough: Duff is informal British English for useless or broken, as in a duff battery.
explanation.definitionFit: A dyestuff is any substance used for dyeing, which is exactly what a colourant is.

clue.text: Gamble from composer dropping name

indicators.note: the composer drops a letter standing for 'name', losing it from his surname

blocks.note: Richard Wagner, German opera composer
standard abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A composer's name disappears from a programme after some kind of gamble.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the N from WAGNER and the German composer becomes a bet.
explanation.definitionFit: A wager is a bet placed on an uncertain outcome, the noun equivalent of a gamble.

clue.text: Smart about appeal, fairly well placed

indicators.note: 'smart' goes about, or around, the word for 'appeal'

blocks.note: to smart is to sting, as a cut does
IT is old slang for sex appeal
pretty good means fairly good

explanation.surface: Someone well dressed and appealing is reckoned to be in a fairly good position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smart' looks like the adjective for well dressed, but it is the verb, as a cut smarts; 'appeal' is the old slang sense of sex appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: Sitting pretty is an idiom for being in a comfortable, advantageous position with nothing to worry about.

clue.text: Unwind remaining part

blocks.note: to unwind is to relax
the remainder, whatever is left over

explanation.surface: Unwinding what is left of a spool of thread.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pairs the two senses as if one thing is unwound, but each half is a definition of its own.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means relax after effort; as a noun it means whatever is left over once some is taken.

clue.text: Run into trouble over testimony lacking weight and expertise

indicators.note: 'run' is put into the word for 'trouble'
the testimony is lacking the letter standing for 'weight', so that letter goes
in a down clue, one piece placed over another sits above it, so it comes first

blocks.note: fuss or bother, as in much ado about nothing
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for run
to bear witness is to give testimony
standard abbreviation for weight

explanation.surface: A witness gets into difficulty when their testimony lacks weight and expert backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run into trouble' reads as a phrase meaning get into difficulty, but it is an instruction: put the run inside the trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Adroitness is skill and cleverness in handling things, a close synonym of expertise.

clue.text: Seabird's wings in storybook turning gold

indicators.note: the wings of a word are its two ends, so keep only the outside letters of 'storybook'
the symbol for 'gold' is turning round to face the other way

blocks.note: first and last letters of the word
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A seabird in a children's story spreads its wings and its feathers turn golden.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-S reads as 'has': the seabird has these pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The skua is a large, predatory seabird of northern and southern oceans that harries gulls for food.

clue.text: Outfit infiltrated by devious mole supported by engineers in distance

indicators.note: devious means crooked or indirect, so the letters of 'mole' go crooked
the outfit is infiltrated, so the jumbled 'mole' gets inside it
in a down clue, a piece supported by another has that other beneath it, so it follows

blocks.note: a kit is a set of clothes or equipment
the letters to be rearranged
the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: A spy ring, with a devious mole inside and engineers in support, operating at a distance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mole' and 'outfit' paint an espionage scene, but the mole is just four letters to shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: A kilometre is a unit of length, a thousand metres, so it names a distance.

clue.text: Passionate in study, enthralled by technique

indicators.note: to be enthralled by something is to be held captive by it, so 'study' is held inside 'technique'

blocks.note: an art is a skill or technique
a den is a private room for study

explanation.surface: A student so passionate about learning that they are enthralled by technique.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Study' is the room, not the act of learning: a den is a study.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardent means burning with enthusiasm or feeling, a straightforward synonym of passionate.

clue.text: Crew took food according to report

indicators.note: a report is what is heard, so we want the word as it is heard, not as written

blocks.note: took food means consumed a meal, past tense

explanation.surface: A report that the crew stopped to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crew' reads as sailors on a ship, but here it is a rowing crew, which in a racing shell numbers eight.
explanation.definitionFit: In rowing, an eight is a boat for eight oarsmen, and by extension the team of rowers who man it.

clue.text: Get lost, drained and muddled

blocks.note: scram is a curt order to go away
bled dry means drained

explanation.surface: Someone lost, exhausted and confused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get lost' is an imperative here, the rude dismissal SCRAM, not a description of losing your way.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrambled describes things jumbled up or thrown into disorder, like a confused message, which is muddled.

clue.text: Display from person providing website's latest post

indicators.note: the latest letter of 'website' is its final one

blocks.note: a man is a person
providing that means if
the final letter of website
a post is a station, as in a guard's post

explanation.surface: Someone puts on a show by writing the newest post on a website.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Post' suggests a blog entry, but it is the place you are stationed; 'providing' is IF, as in 'providing it rains'.
explanation.definitionFit: A manifestation is an outward sign or showing of something, so it can stand for a display.

clue.text: Track back and pinch vegetable

indicators.note: going back, the word for 'track' is read from right to left

blocks.note: a rut is a track worn by wheels
to nip is to pinch

explanation.surface: Someone retraces their steps and steals a vegetable from the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pinch' could mean steal, but here it is a nip, a squeeze between the fingers.
explanation.definitionFit: The turnip is a root crop with a round white bulb, eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Stocked by fantastic inn, amontillado's spicy stuff

indicators.note: the answer is stocked by, held in, the run of words that follows

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of the first word through the second into the third

explanation.surface: A wonderful inn stocks sherry and spices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fantastic' looks like it should shuffle 'inn', but it is only part of the letter string.
explanation.definitionFit: Cinnamon is a warm spice from tree bark, used in baking and mulled drinks.

clue.text: Sailor, leader of heroes previously, admitting sin, raised disgust

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter
in a down clue, raising a word turns it upside down, so it reads bottom to top
to admit is to let in, so 'previously' lets in 'sin'

blocks.note: able-bodied seaman
first letter
once means formerly
to err is to sin

explanation.surface: A sailor, once a leader of heroes, confesses his wrongdoing and provokes revulsion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Previously' is the word being entered, not a time marker for the sailor; 'raised' applies to the sin, which reads upward in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Abhorrence is a feeling of loathing or repugnance, which is what disgust also names.

clue.text: Extra nervous beginner, last of intake in row taken round

indicators.note: nervous means jittery, so the letters of 'beginner' and its companion jitter into a new order
the last of a word is its final letter
taken round means turned about, so the word for 'row' reads backwards
the jumbled group goes in the word for 'row'

blocks.note: a tiff is a minor quarrel
the word itself is the fodder
the final letter

explanation.surface: An extra-nervous newcomer, the last to be taken on, is brought round in a row.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' rhymes with cow here: a quarrel, TIFF, which turns round to FFIT and wraps the shuffled letters after its first F.
explanation.definitionFit: A fringe benefit is a perk given on top of wages, such as a company car, so it is an extra.

clue.text: We think differently about number possessing inside information

indicators.note: the words 'we think' are arranged differently
the rearranged letters go about, around, the abbreviation for 'number'

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
No. is the standard abbreviation for number

explanation.surface: Those who think otherwise about a figure claim to have insider knowledge.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of WE THINK rearrange around NO, which sits just before the final W.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in the know is an idiom for being well informed about things others are not told.

clue.text: Learner in shift working for club

indicators.note: the learner goes in the word for 'shift'

blocks.note: to budge is to shift slightly
L is the learner-driver plate
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: A trainee on a work shift at a club, perhaps a golf or social club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Club' suggests an organisation, but it is the heavy stick; 'shift' is the verb, not a spell of work.
explanation.definitionFit: A bludgeon is a thick heavy stick used as a weapon, and a club is that same kind of cudgel.

clue.text: Cat getting little horse so agitated

indicators.note: agitated means stirred up, so the letters of the preceding words are stirred into a new order

blocks.note: all thirteen letters are the fodder

explanation.surface: A cat's arrival makes a pony nervous.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole run 'little horse so' is used letter for letter; 'little' is not a cue to shorten anything.
explanation.definitionFit: A tortoiseshell is a domestic cat whose mottled coat of black, orange and cream resembles the shell of a tortoise.

clue.text: Study of plants in colour occupying child

indicators.note: to occupy is to take up space within, so 'colour' sits inside 'child'

blocks.note: a boy is a male child
tan is a light brown colour

explanation.surface: A child absorbed in colouring in pictures of plants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Colour' suggests crayons, but it asks for a named shade, here a light brown.
explanation.definitionFit: Botany is the branch of biology concerned with plant life, its structure and classification.

clue.text: Open with silly run, upset

indicators.note: silly means foolish or disordered, so the letters of 'run' are put in a disordered sequence

blocks.note: overt means done openly, not hidden
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A cricketer opens the batting, runs out foolishly, and is upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Open' is the adjective OVERT, not the verb; the definition 'upset' is the verb, to knock over.
explanation.definitionFit: To overturn something is to tip it over, and to upset a vase or a boat means the same.

clue.text: Hurtful obstacle followed by plot

indicators.note: the obstacle comes first and is followed by the plot

blocks.note: a bar is a barrier or obstacle
a bed is a plot of ground in a garden, as in a flower bed

explanation.surface: A painful setback followed by a scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plot' reads as a scheme or story, but it is a patch of garden.
explanation.definitionFit: A barbed remark carries a hidden sting meant to wound, like a hook with barbs, so it is hurtful.

clue.text: Live group, harassed

blocks.note: to be is to exist or live
a set is a group

explanation.surface: A band playing live, hounded by fans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Live group' suggests a band on stage, but 'live' is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Beset means troubled or attacked on all sides, as in beset by problems, which is being harassed.

clue.text: Agreement necessary to provide alibi

indicators.note: the answer is a necessary part of, contained in, the following words

blocks.note: the letters straddle the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: An accomplice agrees to give someone an alibi.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters straddle the break between 'provide' and 'alibi'.
explanation.definitionFit: A deal is an arrangement or bargain struck between parties, which is an agreement.

clue.text: Article, canny one stirring anger

indicators.note: stirring mixes things round, so the letters of 'canny one' are mixed into a new order

blocks.note: the indefinite article
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece by a shrewd writer that stirs up fury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canny' is Scottish and northern English for shrewd; here it is just letters to mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Annoyance is irritation or vexation, a milder shade of the same feeling as anger.

clue.text: Question for children

blocks.note: a matter under debate
a legal word for offspring

explanation.surface: A quiz question set for kids.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Children' as issue is a legal and formal usage, as in 'died without issue'.
explanation.definitionFit: An issue is a point in dispute; in law and old usage it also means a person's offspring or descendants.

clue.text: Sailing boat left course, going west

indicators.note: in an across clue, going west means reading right to left

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for left
a way is a route or course

explanation.surface: A sailing boat leaves its course and heads west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks like the past tense of leave, but it is the direction.
explanation.definitionFit: A yawl is a two-masted sailing vessel with a small mizzen mast set behind the rudder post.

clue.text: Healthy and popular, with good weight? Capital

blocks.note: in good health
in fashion
standard abbreviation for good
a ton is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: A healthy, well-liked person of sound weight is praised as capital, meaning excellent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital?' reads as an exclamation of approval; it is a nation's seat of government.
explanation.definitionFit: Wellington is the seat of government of New Zealand, making it that country's capital city.
